questions.q: In Scenario 1, what is the recommended first step when a cost center controller says an expense balance looks too high?
options: Immediately reverse all journals posted to that account
Use Inquire on Detail Balances to confirm the actual figure and rule out a PTD/YTD misread before assuming the balance is really wrong
Permanently close the period
Run a full consolidation
questions.explain: The least invasive first step is confirming the actual balance and time frame, since a PTD/YTD mix-up is one of the most common false alarms (lesson 22).

questions.q: Once Scenario 1 confirms the balance is genuinely high, what does Account Inspector add that a flat balance inquiry cannot?
options: It deletes the unwanted balance
It automatically fixes the journal entries
It only works on income statement accounts, never balance sheet accounts
It lets the total be pivoted by cost center or other segments, isolating whether the overage is concentrated in one area
questions.explain: Account Inspector's pivot capability (lesson 24) is exactly what isolates where an overage is really concentrated.

questions.q: In Scenario 2, what must happen before changing a blocked period's status actually represents a true close?
options: Nothing — the status can be changed regardless of unposted journals
Only manual journals need to be checked; imported and recurring journals are irrelevant
The next fiscal year must already be open
Every unposted and error journal for that period, across every source, must be found and resolved first
questions.explain: As lesson 34 covered, closing the period doesn't resolve pending journals — they must be cleared first for the close to be meaningful.

questions.q: In Scenario 3, why is it important to confirm revaluation already ran before concluding intercompany balances are mismatched?
options: Revaluation is unrelated to intercompany balances
Revaluation permanently deletes intercompany accounts
An un-revalued foreign-currency intercompany balance can look mismatched even when the underlying balances aren't actually a real problem
Revaluation is only relevant during year-end close
questions.explain: Without revaluation applied, a foreign-currency intercompany pair may appear out of balance simply due to unadjusted exchange rate movement, not a genuine error.

questions.q: What course comes next after General Ledger in the Oracle Fusion Financials Consultant path's Financials Configuration stage?
options: Oracle Fusion Cash Management
Oracle Fusion Security
SQL for Oracle Financials
Accounts Payable
questions.explain: Accounts Payable is next in the Financials Configuration stage, following Enterprise Structures & Chart of Accounts and General Ledger.
